owners.name: Palo Alto Networks
owners.notes: Ignite on Tour is Palo Alto Networks’ vendor event series. Vendor sponsorship economics differ from independent events.

owners.name: Cybertech / Arrowmedia Israel
owners.notes: Cybertech’s official consent notice identifies Cybertech group entities including Arrowmedia Israel. Regional legal contracting entities can vary; this record groups the event producer, not its sponsors.

owners.name: Corinium Global Intelligence
owners.notes: CISO Sydney’s official site and contact details identify Corinium as the event producer.

owners.name: Gartner
owners.notes: Gartner’s official conference portfolio identifies its Cybersecurity & Risk Management Summits. The existing Gartner event-specific imports are preserved as separate legacy records.

owners.name: heise conferences GmbH
owners.notes: secIT’s legal imprint identifies heise conferences GmbH, a heise group company.

owners.name: Linux Foundation / CNCF
owners.notes: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon is CNCF’s flagship conference delivered through Linux Foundation Events. Broad cloud-native attendance includes security practitioners; this is adjacent competition.

owners.name: Billington CyberSecurity
owners.notes: Billington’s official events portfolio identifies its government-focused summits.

owners.name: IAPP
owners.notes: IAPP produces the Global Summit for privacy, AI governance, and cybersecurity law professionals.

owners.name: RSA Conference LLC (RSAC)
owners.notes: The official legal notices identify RSA Conference LLC. Do not conflate this producer with the RSA security software business.

owners.name: SANS Institute
owners.notes: SANS publishes and runs its training events and summits. Training-led formats compete partially for practitioner education budgets.

owners.name: ISACA
owners.notes: ISACA’s official conference portfolio identifies North America, Europe, and GRC conferences. The GRC event is jointly presented with The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA); IIA is a co-organizer, not a sponsor.

owners.name: AFCEA International
owners.notes: AFCEA’s official portfolio lists TechNet events. Government and defense emphasis implies partial or adjacent overlap with CRA.

owners.name: PROIDEA Sp. z o.o.
owners.notes: CONFidence identifies PROIDEA as producer; Oh My Hack also names PROIDEA as organizer, with Zaufana Trzecia Strona providing editorial expertise.

owners.name: ITWeb
owners.notes: ITWeb’s official Security Summit portfolio covers its South African conference series.

owners.name: Cisco
owners.notes: Cisco Live’s official website identifies Cisco Systems. This is a broad vendor and partner event with security programming.

owners.name: RX (Reed Exhibitions)
owners.notes: The official event footer identifies Reed Exhibitions Limited / RX. RELX is identified as the group; event brand names are not treated as separate legal owners.

owners.name: FIRST
owners.notes: FIRST’s official annual conference portfolio documents its incident-response community event.

owners.name: ERNW Enno Rey Netzwerke GmbH
owners.notes: TROOPERS’ official footer identifies ERNW Enno Rey Netzwerke GmbH.

owners.name: OWASP Foundation
owners.notes: OWASP’s official policy identifies Global AppSec conferences as Foundation events. Local AppSec Israel is not assumed to share the same legal organizer without verification.

owners.name: Black Hat
owners.notes: Black Hat’s official footer identifies the Black Hat / Informa Festivals business and Informa PLC. Black Hat MEA has separate co-organizer documentation.

owners.name: DEF CON
owners.notes: DEF CON’s own website documents its flagship conference brand. The speculative Middle East listing is held separately for ownership and occurrence verification.

owners.name: NürnbergMesse GmbH
owners.notes: The official it-sa platform footer identifies NürnbergMesse GmbH.

owners.name: Chaos Computer Club Veranstaltungsgesellschaft mbH
owners.notes: CCC Events links to CCCV’s legal notice. This records the event operating entity rather than presuming every CCC chapter owns the Congress.

owners.name: Fortinet
owners.notes: Fortinet’s official Accelerate article identifies the customer and partner conference.

owners.name: Microsoft
owners.notes: Microsoft’s official Secure and Israel R&D websites identify its vendor events. BlueHat IL’s event details still require date verification.

owners.name: FS-ISAC
owners.notes: FS-ISAC’s official events portfolio identifies its summits and member community; financial-services focus narrows audience overlap.

owners.name: Security BSides Las Vegas, Inc.
owners.notes: The Las Vegas site identifies Security BSides Las Vegas, Inc. Independent BSides chapters are not rolled into a single corporate owner.

owners.name: The Diana Initiative
owners.notes: The Diana Initiative’s official site documents its community conference. It is tracked as a community organizer without an inferred commercial parent.

owners.name: CrowdStrike
owners.notes: CrowdStrike’s official event page documents Fal.Con. It is a vendor-led event with a sponsorship ecosystem.

owners.name: Splunk
owners.notes: Splunk’s official .conf article documents the event and its Cisco relationship.

owners.name: ISC2
owners.notes: ISC2’s official event portfolio identifies Security Congress as its flagship conference.

owners.name: Amazon Web Services
owners.notes: AWS’ official re:Invent website identifies its cloud education and partner event.

owners.name: Payatu Technologies
owners.notes: Nullcon’s official announcement identifies Payatu Technologies as parent of Nullcon and reports ISMG’s majority investment.

owners.name: Synacktiv
owners.notes: Hexacon’s team page identifies Synacktiv as the company supporting and organizing the conference.

owners.name: INCIBE
owners.notes: INCIBE’s official ENISE archive identifies it as the organizing agency. Public-sector events are assessed as adjacent competition, not presumed commercial equivalents.

owners.name: Astrea s.r.l.
owners.notes: The official site distinguishes Clusit as event designer and Astrea as organizer. Clusit is a co-producing association, not Astrea’s parent.

owners.name: Cyber Saiyan
owners.notes: RomHack’s official website identifies non-profit Cyber Saiyan as creator and organizer.

owners.name: HackInBo Group
owners.notes: HackInBo’s official site identifies HackInBo Group. No unverified corporate parent is inferred.

owners.name: Fundacja Academic Partners
owners.notes: The Hack Summit FAQ identifies Academic Partners Foundation and Poland’s Cyber Defence Forces Component Command as joint organizers. The latter is a public-sector co-organizer, not a corporate parent.

owners.name: Evention
owners.notes: Advanced Threat Summit’s official organizer and footer identify Evention. Other editorial partners are not treated as owners without further evidence.

owners.name: Securitum
owners.notes: Mega Sekurak Hacking Party’s official registration and organizer contact use Securitum. Sekurak is the event’s editorial/community brand.

owners.name: Dubai World Trade Centre
owners.notes: GISEC’s official release identifies DWTC as organizer and the UAE Cybersecurity Council as host. GITEX is also a DWTC event; host, venue, and organizer roles are distinguished.

owners.name: Tahaluf
owners.notes: Black Hat MEA identifies Tahaluf and SAFCSP as co-organizers, in association with the global Black Hat team. Tahaluf is a joint venture of Informa PLC, SAFCSP, and EIF; it is not represented as a wholly-owned subsidiary.

owners.name: Tradepass
owners.notes: IndoSec’s official website identifies Tradepass as producer.

owners.name: CloserStill Media
owners.notes: CloserStill’s official event portfolio lists Cyber Security World Asia.

owners.name: Image Engine
owners.notes: GovWare identifies Image Engine as producer and organizer. Singapore International Cyber Week is the wider programme; this combined workbook row is not evidence that Image Engine owns all SICW events.

owners.name: ZESUROKU Inc. / CODE BLUE committee
owners.notes: CODE BLUE’s official site identifies its executive committee and ZESUROKU Inc. secretariat. This records the organizing office rather than inferring an unlisted parent.

owners.name: Australian Information Security Association
owners.notes: AISA’s official portfolio identifies CyberCon. CyberConnect Canberra’s official website explicitly identifies AISA as host and provides AISA sponsorship contacts.

owners.name: Information Security Research Association
owners.notes: c0c0n’s official sponsorship information identifies ISRA and Kerala Police as joint organizers. Government collaborators are documented separately from corporate ownership.

owners.name: AUSCERT
owners.notes: AUSCERT is the conference producer and is part of The University of Queensland, as documented in AUSCERT’s official organizational description.

owners.name: Messe Frankfurt Middle East
owners.notes: Intersec’s official contact page places the event in Messe Frankfurt Middle East’s exhibition portfolio. Physical security and fire sectors mean total show attendance is not all cybersecurity attendance.

owners.name: CINI Cybersecurity National Lab
owners.notes: ITASEC’s official call for papers identifies CINI Cybersecurity National Lab as organizer. Local hosts and programme partners are not inferred to be corporate parents.

owners.name: Terrapinn
owners.notes: Terrapinn’s official site and event portfolio identify Identity Week America. The event covers enterprise identity, government identity, and secure credentials.

owners.name: Forward Global
owners.notes: The official INCYBER Forum Europe site identifies Forward Global as organizer.

owners.name: Tel Aviv University
owners.notes: Tel Aviv University identifies Cyber Week as jointly held by its ICRC and Yuval Ne’eman Workshop, the Israeli National Cyber Directorate, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Public-sector co-organizers are documented without treating them as corporate parents.

owners.name: SecWest / Dragos Ruiu
owners.notes: SecWest’s official team page identifies Dragos Ruiu as organizer of CanSecWest. This is not the industrial-security company Dragos, Inc.; no corporate parent is inferred.

owners.name: Comexposium One to One
owners.notes: Comexposium’s official release identifies Comexposium One to One as producer of Les Assises.

owners.name: Pôle d’excellence cyber
owners.notes: Pôle d’excellence cyber lists European Cyber Week among its own programmes. Defense and public-sector partners are not presumed corporate owners.

owners.name: NASK
owners.notes: NASK’s official SECURE conference article explicitly identifies NASK as organizer.

owners.name: BThaber
owners.notes: BThaber’s own registration store lists BZsec event tickets and its editorial event coverage documents the conference.

owners.name: Ciberobs
owners.notes: Ciberobs’ official organizational presentation describes Cyber Africa Forum as its platform, delivered with partners. This does not infer partner organizations as parent companies.

owners.name: Binary Gecko GmbH
owners.notes: OffensiveCon’s current legal imprint identifies Binary Gecko GmbH. Older Blue Frost Security materials are not used to establish current ownership.

owners.name: IDC
owners.notes: IDC’s official events portal identifies IDC as producer of its analyst-led event portfolio. Country-specific event dates remain workbook claims, not newly verified dates.
